summary.text: Quantum mechanics is the fundamental theory describing matter and light, mainly at the scale of atoms and below, where behavior is often counterintuitive.
It explains things classical physics cannot at very small scales, while classical mechanics emerges from it as an approximation at ordinary scales.
Its key features are discrete energy levels, wave-particle duality, and predictions given only as probabilities, and its predictions have been verified to extreme accuracy.

facts.label: Birth
facts.value: Planck's 1900 solution to black-body radiation was an early step

facts.label: Full development
facts.value: The mid-1920s, by Bohr, Schrödinger, Heisenberg, Born, Dirac and others

facts.label: Born rule
facts.value: A probability is the squared size of a probability amplitude

facts.label: Accuracy
facts.value: Quantum electrodynamics matches experiment within 1 part in 10¹²

items.prompt: Why can a marble roll at any speed you like, while an electron in an atom can only hold certain energies?

options.label: Electrons are too heavy to change their energy
Quantum bound states take only discrete energy values
Marbles are made of matter and electrons are not
Energy is never measurable inside an atom

items.explain: Quantum systems have bound states quantized to discrete values of energy and other quantities, unlike classical systems where they vary continuously.

items.prompt: Physicists measure an electron in the same setup many times and get different results, though the setup was identical. What does quantum mechanics say about this?

options.label: The theory gives only probabilities for the outcomes
The equipment must have been faulty each time
The theory predicts one exact result every time
Electrons are not real until a person looks

items.explain: A fundamental feature is that the theory usually cannot predict with certainty what will happen, but only gives probabilities.

items.prompt: A baseball's flight is handled well by classical mechanics. How does that fit with quantum mechanics being more fundamental?

options.label: Classical mechanics is wrong and baseballs are not described
Baseballs must be treated as single atoms to be predicted
Classical mechanics can be derived as an approximation at ordinary scales
Quantum mechanics only applies to light, never to matter

items.explain: Classical mechanics can be derived from quantum mechanics as an approximation valid at ordinary scales.

items.prompt: An experiment shows light sometimes behaves like a particle and sometimes like a wave. What is this called?

options.label: The Born rule
The old quantum theory
Quantum tunneling
Wave-particle duality

items.explain: Measurements of quantum systems show characteristics of both particles and waves, known as wave-particle duality.

items.prompt: The wave function of an electron assigns a number to each point in space. What does squaring its size give you?

options.label: The probability of finding the electron there
The mass of the electron at that point
The temperature of the surrounding region
The exact path the electron will follow

items.explain: Taking the square of the absolute value of the probability amplitude gives a probability, a rule known as the Born rule.

items.prompt: Why did physicists develop quantum mechanics at all, rather than keeping classical physics?

options.label: Classical physics was too accurate for ordinary scales
They found observations classical physics could not explain
They wanted to apply it to human beings first
They set out to prove atoms did not exist

items.explain: It arose gradually from attempts to explain observations such as black-body radiation and the photoelectric effect that classical physics could not reconcile.
